title: Copy-All and Paste to N Letters
statement:
A text field starts with a single letter A. Your editor has only two keys:

  • Copy All copies everything currently in the field to the clipboard. You cannot copy part of the text.
  • Paste appends the clipboard's contents to the field.

Return the fewest key presses needed to end with exactly n letters.

examples.why: Copy, Paste → 2 letters. Copy, Paste, Paste → 6 letters. Five presses in total.
Doubling never reaches 9. Copy, Paste, Paste → 3, then Copy, Paste, Paste → 9.
The field already holds one letter.

hints: After a Copy All, every later Paste adds the same amount. So the length you copied at must divide the final length.
If you copy at length d and paste until n, that phase costs n / d presses (one copy plus n / d − 1 pastes). So cost(n) = min over divisors d of cost(d) + n / d.
Splitting a factor into smaller factors never costs more: a + b ≤ a · b when both are at least 2. So the answer is the sum of n's prime factors, with repeats.

explain.intuition:
Look at the last Copy All. Say the field held d letters then. Every press after it is a Paste of d letters, so d divides n, and that final phase costs n / d presses (the copy plus n / d − 1 pastes). Before it you had to build d letters as cheaply as possible. That gives a clean recurrence over divisors.

The recurrence hides a neat fact. Growing by a factor m costs m presses, and splitting m = a · b into two steps costs a + b, which is never more than a · b for a, b ≥ 2. So you always multiply by primes, and the answer is the sum of the prime factors of n: 12 = 2 · 2 · 3 gives 7.
steps: While d · d ≤ n: while d divides n, add d to presses and divide n by d. Then increase d.
If n > 1 is left, it is a prime factor; add it.
pitfalls: Greedily doubling. It cannot reach odd targets like 9, and it is not optimal in general.
Forgetting the Copy press when counting a phase: multiplying by m costs m presses, not m − 1.
Forgetting the last prime factor larger than √n, so a prime like 997 returns 0.

solutions.title: DP over divisors
solutions.idea: best[i] = min over divisors d of i (d < i) of best[d] + i / d. The last copy happened at length d.

solutions.title: Sum of prime factors
solutions.idea: Multiplying by a composite never beats multiplying by its prime factors one at a time, so add up the prime factors of n with repeats.

followups: Add a third key that deletes one letter. How does that change the search?
Return the actual sequence of key presses, not just the count.
